ambiguity_flags.note: Category A — snapshot boundary. Proposed as replacement for LAYER_2 (the architectural ingestion and snapshot-publication layer) but semantically overlaps with SNAPSHOT_TRUTH (a distinct canonical concept referring to the published artifact state) and risks confusion with OBSERVATIONS (the raw data boundary that Layer-2 is explicitly designed to separate). A 'store' framing implies a data-storage artifact rather than an architectural layer, compounding the conflation risk.

Category D — decision vocabulary. Proposed as replacement for LAYER_3 (an architectural layer whose planned components include Feature Builder, Regime Gate, Supervisor Engine, etc.) but creates direct ambiguity with the decision-vocabulary domain (DecisionPacket, NO_TRADE, guard/trigger/state taxonomies). CLAUDE.md Sections 9 and 10 constitute a constitutional prohibition on implying automated decision or execution capability. Labeling the architectural layer 'decision_layer' would cause downstream governance steps to misclassify architectural-boundary claims as decision-execution claims, affecting enforcement routing.
